intro: Jamaica, birthplace of reggae and Bob Marley, has given the world some of its greatest sprinters.

chapters.title: Taíno and Spanish rule
text: The Taíno called the island Xaymaca, 'land of wood and water'. Spain claimed it after Columbus arrived in 1494.

chapters.title: British Jamaica
text: Britain captured Jamaica in 1655. Sugar plantations used enslaved Africans; Jamaica became one of the richest colonies. Maroons, escaped enslaved people, fought the British and won treaties. Sam Sharpe led a great rebellion in 1831, and slavery ended in 1834–38.

highlight.title: Maroons
highlight.text: The Maroons won self-rule in the mountains in the 1730s.

chapters.title: Independence
text: Jamaica became independent on 6 August 1962. Marcus Garvey, born in Jamaica, inspired Black pride movements worldwide. Hurricane Melissa struck the island hard in October 2025.

keyTerms.meaning: Descendants of people who escaped slavery.
